records.label: Female infant

phenotypes.text: marked reduction of ALA synthetase activity in erythroblasts

quotes: A female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia is described.
A marked reduction of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity of erythroblasts was noticed with and without treatment of pyridoxal phosphate.

records.label: Son (affected brother)
records.segregation: Affected sibs received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus; no ALAS2 mutation found by sequencing
quotes: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth. Their haemoglobin levels were 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl, respectively.
sequence analysis of the ALAS2 gene in the son did not identify any mutations in the coding region, the intron/exon boundaries, or the 1 kb 5' promoter region.

records.label: Patients with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count

variants.as_reported: mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38

quotes: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38

notes.statement: Guernsey et al. (2009) used positional cloning to define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, which they associated with mutations in the SLC25A38 gene.
quotes: Here, by positional cloning, we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia

notes.statement: Guernsey et al. (2009) showed that SLC25A38, an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein, is important for the biosynthesis of heme in eukaryotes.
quotes: demonstrate that SLC25A38 is important for the biosynthesis of heme in eukaryotes

notes.statement: Guernsey et al. (2009) described the sideroblastic anemias as a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired blood disorders. Their morphologic hallmark is ringed sideroblasts, which are bone marrow erythroid precursors with abnormal iron deposits inside their mitochondria.
quotes: The sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematological disorders whose morphological hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts--bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria.

notes.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) concluded that sideroblastic anemia in a family in which a brother and sister of unaffected parents were affected was strongly suggestive of an autosomal recessive trait. The mother had no dimorphic erythrocyte population and showed random X inactivation in peripheral leukocytes, indicating she was not a carrier of an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation.
quotes: Furthermore, the absence of a dimorphic erythrocyte population in the mother, coupled with the demonstration of random X inactivation in her peripheral leucocytes, showed that the mother was not the carrier of any X linked sideroblastic anaemia mutation.
These results strongly suggest that the sideroblastic anaemia in this family is an autosomal recessive trait.

notes.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) excluded ALAS2 as the cause of the sideroblastic anemia in an affected sib pair. Analysis of an intragenic ALAS2 polymorphism showed that the affected sibs had inherited different maternal alleles, and sequencing in the affected son found no mutations in the coding region, intron/exon boundaries, or 1-kb 5-prime promoter.
quotes: Analysis of the inheritance of this intragenic polymorphism showed that the affected sibs received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus, excluding mutations in this gene as the cause of their sideroblastic anaemia.

notes.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) identified a G-to-A transition polymorphism 220 nt 3-prime of the ALAS2 AATAAA polyadenylation signal. Analysis of 148 alleles by mismatch PCR and XmnI restriction digestion gave a gene frequency of 25%.
quotes: A useful polymorphism was found in the 3' region of the ALAS2 gene, a G to A transition, 220 nt 3' of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal. Mismatch PCR at this site and subsequent discrimination by XmnI restriction analysis of 148 alleles identified the gene frequency of this polymorphism to be 25%.

notes.statement: Manabe et al. (1982) found normal mitochondrial neutral protease activity in the erythroblasts of a female infant with congenital pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia. This protease specifically inactivates the apo form of ALA synthetase, and the apoenzyme's sensitivity to it was also normal. They speculated that the low ALA synthetase activity resulted from impaired production of the enzyme rather than faster destruction, which could explain why the patient did not respond to pyridoxine.
quotes: Mitochondrial neutral protease activity of erythroblasts, which inactivates specifically the apo form of ALA synthetase, was normal and the sensitivity of apo form of ALA synthetase to the neutral protease was also normal.

It was speculated that the reduction of ALA synthetase activity is not due to the high speed of destruction, but rather due to the impairment in production of ALA synthetase, which could explain the unresponsiveness to pyridoxine therapy in this case.
